newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-AZHARUDDIN STEERS INDIA OUT OF TROUBLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AZHARUDDIN STEERS INDIA OUT OF TROUBLE.

text.p: Former captain Mohammad Azharuddin scored a stylish 81 to steer India out of trouble and to a total of 239 for seven in their Asia Cup final against world champions Sri Lanka on Saturday.
Azharuddin, who scored an undefeated 81 in the league match against Sri Lanka, followed up with an identical score off 102 balls with two sixes and one four.
He shared a fourth wicket partnership of 109 off 140 balls with skipper Sachin Tendulkar, who had decided to bat first after winning the toss.
Tendulkar (53) hit two fours in his 67 balls innings, as he and Azharuddin rescued India from a shaky position of 59 for three after 18 overs.
India's total would have been much higher had it not been for some excellent fielding by the Sri Lankans.

Roshan Mahanama, one of the finest fielders in the side brought off a superb one-handed catch at mid wicket to send back Rahul Dravid for seven, and there were three other catches that went quite close to matching it.
Ruwan Kalpage made a lot of ground at long on to hold a huge drive by Tendulkar.
Azharuddin departed to another brilliant effort by Muthiah Muralitharan who ran along the long-on boundary to dive sideways and pluck the ball from the air.
Aravinda de Silva made his presence felt with two diving catches to send back Saurav Ganguly for 34 and Robin Singh for nine.
